NDT software in Fort McMurray: running inspection work from camp

Fort McMurray and the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo sit at the centre of Canada's oil sands. North of town are the mining and upgrading operations: Suncor's Base Plant, Syncrude's Mildred Lake site, Canadian Natural's Horizon, Imperial's Kearl and the Fort Hills mine. South and east are in-situ SAGD facilities with steam generators, well pads and long runs of pipe. Most of the inspection work here is done by crews on rotation, flying in or driving up Highway 63, living in camp and working through winters that sit at minus 30 and colder for weeks.

For an NDT company working in Fort McMurray, the challenge is not finding work. It is keeping certificates, instruments, reports and billing straight when the people doing the work are hundreds of kilometres from the office, change every rotation, and hand over mid-job. The Atlantis ERP solution is one system configured for NDT and inspection companies, covering certifications, dispatch, instruments and calibration, NDT reports, timesheets and invoicing. It is affordable, accessible from a camp room or a site trailer, and fully customized. Demo and quote on request.

ERP for NDT companies in Fort McMurray: what rotational work needs

An ERP for NDT companies in Fort McMurray has to be built around handovers. When one crew flies out and another flies in, the incoming technicians need to know which jobs are open, which instruments are on site, which reports are still in draft and what the client is expecting. The Atlantis ERP keeps all of that in one database, split into apps that match NDT work.

  • Team Assignments with an availability calendar that holds rotations, leave and training.
  • NDT Reports with an offline field app that syncs when a connection is available.
  • Asset Management for instruments kept at site, issued and returned between crews.
  • Certificates so no one is flown in on an expired certificate.
  • Timesheets, Expenses and Invoicing for travel, standby, inspection time and field costs.

Supporting apps include Procedures, Project, Inventory, Purchase, Maintenance and Dashboards.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software built around camp rotations

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for Fort McMurray has to understand that a technician's availability is set months ahead by their rotation. In Team Assignments, the technician availability calendar holds assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable entries, and overlaps are blocked. Rotation days off can be entered as leave or unavailable blocks during setup, so dispatch cannot book someone into a site on their days out.

Each job moves through planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed, with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates. On sites where the gate, the camp and the work area are separate locations kilometres apart, GPS coordinates reduce first-day confusion. Equipment serial numbers cannot be double-booked, and the dispatcher is warned if an assigned instrument is out of calibration, which is worth knowing before a crew flies north rather than after.

Technician status, current assignment, utilisation and next available date appear in calendar, kanban and list views. For a coordinator in Edmonton or Calgary covering a Fort McMurray scope, that is the difference between a clean crew change and a missing Level II on a Monday morning. The Project app records safety induction and work permit fields per job, so site orientations completed by each crew are visible when planning the next rotation.

NDT reporting software that works offline in the oil sands

NDT reporting software for Fort McMurray must work where the network does not. Camp Wi-Fi may be fine, but inside a mine site, an upgrader unit or out on a SAGD well pad, a technician often has no usable signal. The Atlantis field app is an installable web app that works without signal: it stores report drafts and photos on the device, offers a method picker, photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview, and syncs back when a connection returns.

The ERP covers 17 report types, including UT thickness with readings by direction for wear surveys on piping, PAUT with focal laws and TOFD for welds, MFL with scan mode for tank floors, IRIS and ECT for exchanger tubes, and PMI, hardness and PWHT reports for alloy work during upgrader turnarounds. RT reports capture source, technique and IQI details; MT and PT reports capture technique, particle type, method and developer. Weld and job lines record defect type and orientation, and each report gives an overall result.

Reports run through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures. That lets a Level II in the field submit and a Level III review from the office the same day, which matters on a turnaround with a tight window. Reports are issued on versioned company templates in PDF, Word, Excel or HTML, and Excel formats demanded by operators are filled automatically by mapping fields to cells. See Digital Twin Reporting Software and, for 3D views of indications and thickness data, Atlantis Digital Twins.

Calibration management software for instruments that stay at site

In Fort McMurray, instruments often stay at site while people rotate. That breaks paper sign-out sheets: nobody knows which of the incoming crew took the flaw detector, and a probe damaged by the cold goes back on the shelf without a note. Calibration management software needs to follow the instrument, not the person.

The Atlantis ERP tracks each instrument, probe and source-related item by serial number, with assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories and lifecycle status. Issue and return requires supervisor and manager approval, and condition is recorded at issue and at return, so damage is attributed to the right rotation. Reservations prevent clashes when two scopes want the same unit, and inbound and outbound movements are logged when equipment moves between the city shop and site.

Calibration records hold provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, result and next due date; the certificate register tracks valid, expiring and expired status and sends alerts. The maintenance log records repairs, cleaning, firmware updates and probe replacement with condition before and after, which is how you see that cold-weather cable failures keep hitting the same kit. Consumables such as low-temperature couplant, MT and PT chemicals and PPE carry reorder levels and a low-stock flag, because running out mid-rotation means a supply run on Highway 63.

Technician certification tracking software before anyone flies north

Technician certification tracking software should catch an expiring certificate before the flight, not at the site gate. The Atlantis ERP computes certificate status automatically as active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked, and creates warning tasks 90 days ahead. Configurable email alerts go to the people planning the next rotation, with the look-ahead days and resend interval you choose.

Each record holds scheme, level, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT and training hours, exam result and attachments. Canadian technicians typically hold ISO 9712 certificates through the national program administered by the Canadian General Standards Board (previously NRCan); crews brought in from elsewhere may carry SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, PCN or CSWIP, and all are recorded in one register. Vision tests are tracked with Jaeger near vision, far vision, colour perception, examiner, clinic and expiry.

The employee NDT profile holds highest level, methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, and timesheets warn when a technician without a valid certificate logs hours. If you train people under a written practice, Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based courses through eLearning, which crews can work through from camp on their own devices; other schemes are recorded, not taught.

Procedures and operator requirements in the Wood Buffalo region

Oil sands operators run large, tightly managed contractor programs, and most have their own requirements on top of provincial rules. ABSA governs pressure equipment in Alberta, and the Alberta Energy Regulator oversees oil sands mining and in-situ operations. For an NDT contractor, the practical result is that the procedure you work to must be the approved revision, and you must be able to prove it.

The Procedures app keeps a register with document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria and body text or an uploaded file. Procedures go through draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, and approved revisions are locked, with a snapshot of each revision kept. Reports reference the procedure used, so the chain from report back to controlled document is intact.

An AI-assisted first draft helps when an operator asks for a site-specific procedure at short notice; a Level III still reviews and approves it. NCR and CAPA workflows can be configured during implementation for contractors who need to track client nonconformance reports alongside their own.

Timesheets, expenses and NDT invoicing software for rotational work

NDT invoicing software for Fort McMurray has to bill what rotational work actually costs. Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), method, site, client, equipment serial, billable flag and rate multiplier, with approval before billing. Travel days, standby while a unit is being made safe, and overtime premiums all land on the timesheet with the right multiplier instead of in a supervisor's notebook.

Expenses handle per diems, flights where the client reimburses them, and field purchases, re-billed to the job. Quotations carry job type, site, project dates, applicable codes and NDT service products by method and category, with a branded PDF and online acceptance that converts to a sales order.

Invoices carry the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with subtotals for labour, equipment and consumables and lines showing cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours. Operators' payables teams tend to reject invoices that do not match their PO and timesheet data, and this level of line detail is what gets an invoice through. GST and payment terms are configured during implementation, and the financial dashboard tracks revenue, gross margin, EBITDA and outstanding invoices over twelve months.

Inspection management software for Fort McMurray: dashboards and integration

Inspection management software lets the office run a site it cannot see. Dashboards show certificates expiring and expired, calibration due and overdue, and issued equipment overdue for return, which in a rotational operation is the list to check at every crew change. The financial dashboard sits beside it.

Oil sands operators run large enterprise maintenance and procurement systems. The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation. Field devices use the same API to list the jobs assigned to a technician and the equipment issued to them, and to submit and sync reports. Discuss and Calendar keep office and site talking between shifts, and Surveys can collect client feedback at the end of a campaign.

Affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Fort McMurray: implementation

An affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Fort McMurray is configured around your rotation pattern, your site instrument pools and your operator clients. Atlantis NDT sets up and supports the system; pricing is quote on request.

  1. Rotation setup. Rotation schedules entered into the availability calendar so dispatch respects days out.
  2. Site equipment pools. Instruments at each site loaded with serials, calibration history and condition.
  3. Templates. Report and invoice layouts that match each operator's requirements.
  4. Field devices. The offline app installed and tested on the tablets crews actually carry, including a no-signal test.
  5. Crew-change checks. Dashboard views agreed for each handover: open reports, issued equipment, upcoming expiries.

Best NDT software for small NDT companies working in Fort McMurray

Smaller contractors in Wood Buffalo often run one or two crews on long-term operator contracts. For them, the best NDT software removes the evening admin in camp. A typical starting set is NDT Reports with the offline app, Certificates, Asset Management and Timesheets feeding Invoicing. Ask for a quote for a small Fort McMurray contractor or ask how offline reporting works on your devices.

Frequently asked questions

Does the NDT reporting app work with no cell signal at an oil sands site?

Yes. The installable field app stores drafts and photos locally and syncs when a connection returns, with photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview available offline.

Can the scheduling software handle camp rotations?

Yes. Rotation days out can be entered in the technician availability calendar, and overlapping bookings are blocked.

How do we track instruments that stay at site between crews?

Each instrument is tracked by serial number with issue and return approval and condition recorded at both ends, so equipment passes between rotations with a record.

Can it record ISO 9712 certificates from the Canadian program?

Yes, along with SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, PCN and CSWIP. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only.

Can it connect to an operator's SAP or Maximo system?

Yes. The open REST API integrates with SAP, Maximo and other systems that accept API connections, with scope agreed during implementation.

What does it cost?

Pricing is quote on request, based on apps, templates, integrations and number of crews. The goal is affordable, accessible and fully customizable.
